q: p = 0.03 means a 3% chance that the null hypothesis is true.
why: Myth. It's the chance of data at least this extreme IF the null were true.

q: Not rejecting H₀ proves that H₀ is true.
why: Myth. It only means the data aren't strong enough against it. A small sample often can't tell.

q: The true effect is small. As the sample grows, the p-value tends to…
why: More data shrink the SE, so even a small real effect stands out.

q: A statistically significant result is practically important.
why: With huge samples, tiny effects become significant. Always look at the size of the effect too.

q: You test 20 true null hypotheses at the 5% level. How many do you expect to come out significant by chance?
why: 20 × 0.05 = 1. This is why many tests need care.
